title: Scribe v3 MCP Explained: Benchmarks, Pricing, and Specs
summary: Scribe v3 MCP provides an integration bridge for AI agents to retrieve and execute automated process documentation directly within their workflows.
body_markdown:
## Scribe v3 MCP is direct access to process documentation for AI agents


### The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standard


Eliminating the need for custom-built integrations between specific AI models and disparate data sources is the primary role of the Model Context Protocol. In a traditional setup, a human must copy text from a browser into a chat interface.


This introduces latency and formatting errors that degrade the model’s ability to follow complex instructions.


By establishing this direct connection, a model like Claude Opus 5.5 can pull the exact "how-to" steps it needs to complete a task autonomously. Consequently, the documentation becomes a functional API for the agent's reasoning loop rather than just a visual aid for a person.


### Defining scribe as an asr foundation


Scribe v3 is an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model designed to transcribe recorded audio, including meetings, customer calls, and support conversations, with high accuracy. Unlike earlier speech recognition tools built for human readers, this system processes raw audio streams to generate high-fidelity transcripts for agentic consumption.


> Consequently, the documentation becomes a functional API for the agent's reasoning loop rather than just a visual aid for a person.


It serves as the bridge between spoken technical instructions and the structured data required by the Model Context Protocol.


The architecture relies on a deep neural network optimized for technical jargon and multi-speaker environments. By focusing on speech-to-text accuracy, Scribe v3 ensures that the documentation fed into an AI agent is free from the phonetic errors that typically break automated reasoning loops.


### Scribe v3 MCP vs. Scribe screen capture extension


Readers familiar with the popular Scribe browser extension for screen-capture guides should note that Scribe v3 is a distinct technological pivot. While the legacy tool already provided speech recognition for human readers, v3 is an audio-first engine built for machine consumption.


This version does not replace the click-capture tool but rather introduces a new infrastructure for converting spoken expertise into agentic memory.


The transition from visual guides to ASR-based documentation reflects the shift toward agents that "listen" to technical requirements rather than "watching" a UI.


By prioritizing audio streams, Scribe v3 captures the underlying logic and verbal nuances that are often missing from a series of silent screenshots.


### How v3 differs from previous API integrations


Developers were previously required to write specific "glue code" to translate raw Scribe API JSON data into a format that a Large Language Model could understand.


With v3, the system natively exposes documentation as tools that models like GPT-6.2 Astra can see and call as if they were internal functions.


Activepieces runs as a per-project MCP server, so Claude, Cursor or Windsurf can create, edit and explain a flow without you ever opening a separate builder UI.


This moves beyond a chat interface that merely explains a UI, granting the agent CRUD control to execute changes that are immediately visible in the run trace.


To verify the depth of this control, connect Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Windsurf to the MCP server endpoint, ask it to build or modify a flow, and read the tool calls and resulting changes in the run trace.


### Key technical specifications as of late 2025


High-frequency polling and structured retrieval form the core of the Scribe v3 infrastructure, supporting the long-horizon agentic work required by modern frontier models.


Standard JSON-RPC over Stdio or HTTP serves as the transport layer for compatibility with local IDEs and cloud-based agent environments. The resource templates are URI-based access points to specific Scribe folders. These allow administrators to restrict an agent's knowledge to relevant departments.


Tool definitions map Scribe steps to executable schemas. This allows models like Gemini 4 Carbon to verify completion of each step in a sequence.
